question: What is a key advantage of batch processing?
options: It guarantees sub-millisecond latency for every record
High throughput and efficient use of resources when processing large volumes of data together
It eliminates the need to store any data
It requires no computing resources at all
explanation: Batch processing offers high throughput and resource efficiency for large data volumes. It does not provide sub-millisecond latency, remove storage needs, or run without compute.

question: Why is batch processing often more cost-effective than continuous streaming for suitable workloads?
options: Because it never uses any hardware
Because streaming is always free
Because compute can be provisioned to run at scheduled times (e.g., off-peak) rather than kept running continuously
Because batch jobs never fail
explanation: Scheduling batch jobs (e.g., off-peak) avoids paying for always-on streaming infrastructure. Batch still uses hardware, streaming is not free, and batch jobs can fail like any process.

question: How does batch processing simplify error handling compared to some streaming systems?
options: Errors are impossible in batch jobs
A failed batch can often be re-run over the same bounded dataset, making reprocessing and debugging more straightforward
Batch systems automatically fix all data errors
Batch jobs cannot be monitored
explanation: Because a batch operates on a bounded dataset, a failed run can typically be re-executed, easing reprocessing and debugging. Errors are still possible, not auto-fixed, and batch jobs can be monitored.

question: Which advantage explains why batch processing is well suited to complex, resource-intensive transformations?
options: It can leverage large parallel compute over the entire dataset at once, optimizing heavy joins and aggregations
It forbids any joins or aggregations
It only runs on a single CPU core
It requires the dataset to fit in a single cell
explanation: Batch can apply large-scale parallel compute across a whole dataset, optimizing heavy joins and aggregations. It permits joins/aggregations, uses many cores, and handles large datasets.

question: Which statement best summarizes an advantage of batch processing for large historical datasets?
options: It cannot handle historical data
It processes each record only in real time and discards history
It efficiently handles very large historical volumes in a single coordinated run, maximizing throughput per unit of compute
It requires manual entry of every record
explanation: Batch efficiently crunches large historical volumes in one coordinated, high-throughput run. It does handle history, does not discard it, and does not require manual data entry.
